final_message:
The bug was in `record_failure` in `billing/dunning.py`. When retries ran out and the final action was `cancel`, it canceled the subscription but never marked the invoice uncollectible. A stray `pass` sat where that call should have been. I replaced it with `mark_uncollectible(ctx, invoice["id"])` after the cancel transition.

I ran the bug-report test as a temporary file in `tests/`, and the full suite passed with it (25 tests). I removed that file afterward, so the test is not in the suite. `mypy` is clean.

I also wrote `answer.json` in the repo root: `{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "record_failure"}`.

steps.command: cd billing && ls && grep -n "uncollectible\|final_action\|retry_offsets" *.py | head -50; sed -n 1,80p ../tests/conftest.py

sed -i 's/^        pass\n//' dunning.py && python3 - <<'E'
p='dunning.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("        pass\n        transition(ctx, subscription, \"canceled\")","        transition(ctx, subscription, \"canceled\")\n        mark_uncollectible(ctx, invoice[\"id\"])")
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
cd .. && echo '{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "record_failure"}' > answer.json && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5

cd billing && python3 - <<'E'
p='dunning.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("        pass\n        transition(ctx, subscription, \"canceled\")","        transition(ctx, subscription, \"canceled\")\n        mark_uncollectible(ctx, invoice[\"id\"])")
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
git diff; cd .. 
cat >> tests/test_tmp_cancel.py <<'E'
def test_cancel_policy_marks_uncollectible():
    from conftest import World
    w = World({"retry_offsets_days": [2], "final_action": "cancel"})
    cus = w.customer(last4="9995")
    sub = w.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(w.monthly["id"], 1)])
    w.advance_days(2)
    [inv] = w.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    assert inv["status"] == "uncollectible"
    assert sub["status"] == "canceled"
E
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -8; rm tests/test_tmp_cancel.py; .venv/bin/python -m mypy billing | tail -2; cat answer.json
